result.title: RAN-JEPA: An Action-Conditioned World Model for Energy-efficient Mobile Network Control
result.summary: Operational mobile networks are rich in observations but poor in interventions: they continuously generate large volumes of passive telemetry, while controlled action--response trajectories remain comparatively scarce and costly to collect. This observation--intervention asymmetry is a central obstacle to building practical world models for RAN control. We address this problem with RAN-JEPA, an action-conditioned world model that separates representation learning from intervention learning. The model first learns a predictive latent representation from observation-only network data, adapts that representation to the target deployment domain, and then learns action-conditioned latent dynamics from controlled sleep/wake trajectories while keeping the encoder fixed. We evaluate RAN-JEPA using public operator performance data for pretraining and a real-equipment four-cell 5G testbed for domain adaptation, post-training, and control. Across four future 15-minute intervals, RAN-JEPA achieves lower action-conditioned prediction error than a GPT-2 world-model baseline and a mechanistic rule, while remaining close to a strong persistence reference. What-if evaluation further shows that the model produces distinct and coherent future trajectories under matched SLEEP and KEEP plans. In closed-loop control, RAN-JEPA consistently supports higher sleep ratios than the two baselines at comparable congestion cost. These results show that observation-first, action-conditioned learning can turn abundant passive telemetry and limited intervention data into a practical predictive model for energy-aware RAN control.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 RAN-JEPA，一个动作条件世界模型：先用纯观测的运营商数据学习预测性 latent 表示并适配目标域，再在固定编码器下用少量 sleep/wake 控制轨迹学习动作条件 latent 动力学，用于移动网络节能控制。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「先学预测表示、再冻结编码器学 latent 动力学」的分阶段训练可供核查 LVR 中状态更新与监督信号的分离设计，尤其冻结编码器是否导致任务必要信息坍缩。
